title: Null Controls Are Necessary but Not Sufficient: Evaluating Acceptance Guards for Scientific Discovery and Interpretability
abstract: arXiv:2610.22445v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Automated discovery systems propose scientific explanations and test which to accept. Does passing a test establish the intended claim? We develop four executable operations for changing physical descriptions: identifying redundancies (L1), coarse-graining dynamics (L2), transferring structure (L3), and inferring missing quantities from conservation imbalances (L4). We evaluate these operations and three interpretability settings through null acceptance (NAR), positive acceptance (PAR), and consequence agreement (CAR).   A reduction mapping every state to zero predicts its own future perfectly. It passes closure on 96% of 129 public chaotic systems despite retaining no dynamical variation. An independent observable-preservation test rejects it throughout. On controlled benchmarks, the combined criteria accept 24/24 genuine reductions and reject 72/72 nulls. The other operations distinguish symmetries from redundancies, validate transfers

translated_title: 零控制是必要但非充分的：评估科学发现与可解释性中的接受防护机制
translated_abstract: 自动化科学发现系统会提出科学解释并测试哪些解释应被接受。但通过测试是否就能确立所声称的结论？我们开发了四种用于改变物理描述的可执行操作：识别冗余（L1）、对动力学进行粗粒化（L2）、迁移结构（L3），以及从守恒失衡推断缺失量（L4）。我们通过零接受（NAR）、正接受（PAR）和推论一致性（CAR）三类判据来评估这些操作以及三种可解释性设置。研究发现：一个将每个状态都映射为零的退化约化能够完美预测其自身的未来，尽管不保留任何动力学变化，它却在129个公开混沌系统中的96%上通过了闭合性测试；而一个独立的观测量保持测试则始终将其拒绝。在受控基准上，组合判据接受了全部24个真正的约化（24/24），并拒绝了全部72个零控制（72/72）。其他操作则能够区分对称性与冗余、验证结构迁移（原文在此处截断）。
tldr: 本文提出四种可执行变换操作与三重接受判据（零接受、正接受、推论一致性），证明零控制测试对自动科学发现而言必要但不充分——退化的零映射约化能通过96%混沌系统的闭合性检验，只有结合独立的观测量保持测试，才能可靠地区分真正的科学约化与退化假设。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes four executable transformation operations and three acceptance criteria (null acceptance, positive acceptance, and consequence agreement), demonstrating that null controls are necessary but not sufficient for automated scientific discovery—a degenerate zero-mapping reduction passes closure tests on 96% of chaotic systems, and only by incorporating an independent observable-preservation test can genuine reductions be reliably distinguished from degenerate hypotheses.
